school counselors need to know how to promote the academic development of all students and how to do it.
school counselors can be trained to use a variety of academic interventions to promote academic achievement and to help students develop a positive attitude toward school.
preservice school counselors can learn about and be trained to implement a variety of academic interventions.

the following questions: How does the course prepare preservice school counselors to promote academic development?
the preparation of school counselors to promote academic development.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

school counselors should be prepared to promote student academic success by (1) being aware of the importance of academic development, (2) being knowledgeable of the academic and nonacademic factors that influence student academic development, (3) being knowledgeable of strategies for enhancing student academic development, and (4) being able to implement and evaluate strategies for enhancing student achievement.
preservice school counselor preparation should include the development of a broad understanding of the academic achievement of students in the context of the school and the larger community.
school counselors must be prepared to work with students to develop the skills necessary for academic success.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

school counselors can contribute positively to student achievement by providing leadership in the areas of curriculum and instruction and by developing a comprehensive school counseling program that includes academic support for all students.

school counselor preparation should focus on the development of skills and dispositions that promote student academic success and the ability to work with students, teachers, and parents in the context of the larger school system.

school counselor preparation programs should provide students with a thorough understanding of the academic development process and how it can be enhanced through the application of a range of school counseling interventions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

school counselor preparation programs must include a course on academic development and provide supervised experiences that enable students to develop the skills and dispositions needed for this work.
the preparation of school counselors for this role should be grounded in the knowledge base of academic development and include supervised experiences with students, teachers, and parents.
school counselors must be taught the skills and knowledge needed to promote academic development and that these skills and knowledge should be integrated into their preparation programs.
